items.name: Nocturne bass
items.description: LH broken octave spanning 9th–12th. Low root on beat 1, chord tones spread above. NOT Alberti. Write every LH note explicitly.

items.name: Grace-note entry
items.description: Phrases begin with a grace note leaning into the first structural pitch. The melody breathes before it sings. Combined with rubato, the arrival is never mechanical.

items.name: Chromatic inner voice
items.description: While soprano moves diatonically, a middle voice descends chromatically (often C–B–Bb–A) creating warmth and ache beneath the melody.

items.name: Enharmonic modulation
items.description: Distant key arrived at through a diminished seventh or German augmented sixth respelled. The listener finds themselves somewhere new without a clear "moment of departure."

items.name: Ornamental passagework as melody
items.description: Chromatic runs, cascading sixteenth passages from a peak note are not decoration — they ARE the melody continuing. Do not write them as ornament shorthand; write out every note.

items.name: Brilliant, wide-spanning keyboard figuration

items.name: Abrupt dynamic and registral contrast
items.description: A phrase stated forte in the bass answered piano two octaves up, or a sudden subito piano at a structural arrival. The contrasts are theatrical and placed at joins, not smoothed over.

items.name: Horn-call and folk-dance topics
items.description: Open fifths and thirds in a horn-fifth pattern for the outdoors, and lilting compound-metre or waltz rhythms for the vernacular. These are quotations of a sound-world, and they arrive marked.
